headline: ICE releases Hartford restaurant owner after 12 days in custody
summary: A Hartford restaurant owner detained by ICE was released after Democrat lawmakers' intervention.

headline: Trump administration asks Texas for help providing legal services to immigrant kids facing deportation
summary: Texas border town Roma sees increased presence of asylum seekers, likely due to changing U.S. immigration policies.

headline: No protesters appear for Trump’s Mount Rushmore fireworks six years after clash resulted in arrests
summary: No protests occurred on July 3, 2026, during President Trump's speech and fireworks display at Mount Rushmore. A designated protest area remained empty despite heavy military and law enforcement presence. Native American advocate Nick Tilsen, who led a protest in 2020, said his group NDN Collective was boycotting the event this year to focus on community organizing and avoid feeding into Trump's narrative.

headline: ICE must provide bond hearings within 90 days to detainees awaiting removal decision, 5th Circuit Court of Appeals says
summary: The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that immigrants detained within the country must receive a bond hearing within 90 days, violating their constitutional rights if detained longer without cause. This decision reverses a Trump-era policy enforced by ICE and could impact hundreds of detainees in Mississippi.

headline: ‘Doing nothing was not an option’: NC Senate votes to crack down on hemp
summary: On July 2, 2026, North Carolina Senate passed a bill banning most cannabis products due to health concerns, with bipartisan support. The House will reconvene on July 27 to consider this bill.

headline: Montanans support cigarette tax increase, poll says
summary: A Montana poll found strong bipartisan support for increasing cigarette tax by $2 per pack, with 77% approval and 59% strongly supporting. However, advocates note Montana's high smoking rate and healthcare costs from tobacco use, while opponents argue a higher tax could be regressive.

headline: Michigan lawmakers finalize $85B budget after all-night legislative session
summary: Michigan legislators passed a roughly $85 billion budget for FY2027 after an all-night session, missing the July 1 deadline but avoiding last year's government shutdown. The budget includes cuts to address a $1 billion revenue shortfall but no new taxes. It also increases per-pupil funding in education by $250 to $10,300 and allocates $496.6 million for community colleges, with most seeing increased funding. State departmental funding was reduced overall but maintained key services.
